newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: F&N earnings seen boosted by property.
newsitem.headline: F&N earnings seen boosted by property.

text.p: Diversified food and beverage group Fraser & Neave Ltd (F&N) is expected to report higher profits for 1995/96, with residential property development in Singapore adding much of the gain, analysts said on Thursday.

Analysts polled in The Estimate Directory gave a consensus forecast of S$213 million (US$152 million) in group net profit for the year ended September 30, 1996, an increase of 15 percent over the previous year's S$185 million.
The forecasts range from a low of around S$200 million to a high of S$230 million.
The F&N group is expected to release its results on Friday.

"We don't really expect any surprises from the company. Its core business of making soft drinks is doing well and should continue to do so, but profit will be mainly from the property side," said Lisa Lee, investment analyst with ING Baring Securities.
Property contributions would come mainly from two large residential projects in Singapore, Valley Park and The Anchorage, both located on its former factory sites.
Patrick Yau, investment analyst with Schroders Securities, said he expected property profits to account for more than half of total group profit for the period.
Yau, who forecast net profit of S$230 million for the group, said: "The (profit) figures would vary depending on how much profit they decide to book from their property projects."
Property earnings from subsidiary Centrepoint Properties Ltd should cushion the poor earnings expected from its brewery business held under Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd (APB) .
"We are bearish on the brewery side, especially on their ventures in China, after talking to management," said Danielle Yew, investment analyst with Goldman Sachs.
Yew said she expected earnings for APB to be flat, though some analysts expected a slight decline.
APB's earnings would be dampened by high start-up costs of several joint ventures in China and Thailand, said ING Baring's Lee.
"Their new plant in Hainan will bleed them badly in 1997," said Lee, who has forecasted APB's net profit at S$79.8 million for 1995/96 against S$77.6 million in the previous year.
F&N's core business of soft drinks, which includes a joint venture with Coca Cola, is expected to do well, with strong growth seen especially in Malaysia.
Lee expected the soft drinks business, which contributed pre-tax profit of S$35 million in 1994/95, to see compounded growth of about 30 percent a year over the next three years.
On the group's prospects, analysts said F&N could face a decline in property profits from 1997 after it completed development of its two former factory sites.
"Property earnings are on a decline. The biggest issue is what else they can do to keep their earnings up," said Yau.
Yau, who has a hold recommendation on F&N, said the group would find it difficult to fill the gap left by property earnings.

"The group probably has some land left for development but nothing like the size of Valley Point and The Anchorage. Earnings will be on a decline unless they can come up with something that can pad the big hole left by property," he said.
